# Independent Set44 candidate cutoff reference

This directory derives expected bytes and modeled behavior from the approved Set44 core/helper contracts, clarification 1, and retained independent Set43/condition/manifest inputs. It is outside the repository until the parent explicitly copies the frozen tree. The author has not read new Set44 Go source or output. Go authoring began in parallel after the joint contract freeze; **this directory does not claim its outputs preceded Go authorship**. The semantic reviewer may have implemented the helper, but must review against the contracts without supplying Go-derived expected values.

`input_hashes.json` pins every copied input, including the complete unchanged corrected Set43 reference tree, exact 1,294-byte TZif, the original Set41 stable operation field contract, and the Set44 approval/contracts/formula reports/clarification. The original Set43 tree and all previous reference inputs are unchanged. The generator verifies every input before importing the old independent Python. It never imports project Go, executes project binaries, reruns Argon, renders SVG, mines, or runs statistical studies.

Run `python3 -B reference_event.py --check`. Without `--check`, it writes `event_v1.json`; expected values must never be repaired from implementation output. Python 3.9+ is supported. Calendar values use `ZoneInfo.from_file` on the copied TZif only, and each cutoff/deadline is cross-checked against its exact `PST8PDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0` tail. All 3,861 supported Saturdays and the final 2099-12-26 to 2100-01-02 deadline are included. Host timezone does not select any expected instant.

## Consumer schema

- `rules`: exact object, canonical bytes, framed preimage and RulesID.
- `pin`: exact two-fixture Pin, canonical bytes, framed preimage and StoreID.
- `fixtures`: fixture name, exact entry pin, original public `current_view`, participant ID, and the unchanged three genuine public receipt/assignment/manifest inputs for that gym. Those six receipts were independently normal-Argon verified by the retained earlier reference. They cover middle/light-heavy/heavy, not all five classes.
- `calendar` and `calendar_invalid`: cutoff/deadline arithmetic and invalid date inputs. Calendar Event values contain no admission claim.
- `histories`: full modeled stable/entry operations and assignment inputs, original-operation canonical bytes, each selected fold preimage, final participant snapshot, and its canonical bytes. These journals were constructed independently; they are not captured real database histories. `source_kind` distinguishes genuine immutable receipt inputs from five-class synthetic structural assignments. Synthetic fixtures have no admitted source proof and may only exercise arithmetic/structure or explicitly modeled state.
- `history_cases`: bounded corrupted modeled histories and a pre-cutoff prepared intent resolving after cutoff. Missing-row cases carry `expected_operation_count`, since empty history alone cannot prove loss. `maximum_history` derives the 4,096-row stable/entry endpoints from an explicit recipe; it is not runtime memory or concurrency evidence.
- `records`: complete SnapshotReceipt DTOs, canonical bytes, historical SnapshotInput preimage/digest and whole-evidence receipt preimage/digest. Capture time changes the latter; lawful post-cutoff tails do not change the historical input.
- `dtos`: `{name,kind,fixture,value,canonical}`; includes complete helper unavailable/setup/ready/busy/failed snapshots, queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled jobs, both original views, Info, Record and eight-row metadata History.
- `codec_cases`: `{name,kind,input_hex,accepted,canonical,validation_scope}`. Accepted key-order/whitespace cases are independently checked against their original positive canonical DTO. Core cases include semantic validation under the supplied Pin. Helper cases are **closed transport plus established-pin semantic validation**, not a promise that standalone `ParseEventResponse` without trusted context rejects every authority mismatch. The production parser and command-aware layer jointly establish that boundary. The Python decoder is bounded for finite corpus generation; it does not prove runtime preallocation checks.
- `protocol_cases`: `{name,request,response,fixture,current_view,expected_job,terminal_digest,accepted,canonical}`. Validate response structure and correlate the command, exact current view, Pin/StoreID, date, participant and job. `expected_job` can be queued or an earlier complete terminal job. `terminal_digest` is SHA256 of that whole canonical EventJob. Current-view historical replay is a new job with original capture bytes; prior terminal jobs cannot change even their observation timestamp.
- `initialization_cases`: accepted/refused Create/Open/ResumePrepared states and exact fresh-versus-preserved CreatedAtMS semantics. These are not real filesystem or process-kill tests.
- `scenarios`: semantic actions, expected DTO/error, resulting durable-model summaries, and proof accounting. `expected_proof_count` counts reference-model source visits; it is **not a requirement to waste proof work before a safe early refusal**. `runtime_proof_bounds` allow earlier refusal on failed captures. `state.source_fences` records successful final-fence observations only; initial/metadata source-clock observations are deliberately not a complete model of runtime ClockMS, especially after early source/proof refusal. Explicit delayed/final-boundary runtime tests must still force the relevant late guard; broad failure bounds do not replace them.
- `capacity_case`: 256 reserved rows refuse a new event while an existing row can complete. `bounds` records actual canonical vector sizes and pins the separate conservative formula reports.

## Scope and limitations

The model retains original assignment births and genuine receipt facts. Five-class/retirement vectors deliberately use synthetic assignment facts and never imply a source authority admitted them. No corpus field grants source trust: actual capture must use the concrete pinned source and original authenticated View. Model callbacks represent assumptions about successful proof/lease/write results. Real gates, cancellation joins, LevelDB Sync, partial writes, process kills, scoped test-clock composition and normal shipped-package behavior require separate implementation tests.

All saved IDs remain present with deterministic exclusion (`retired` before `not_rostered`). Original historical session/operation bytes remain in folds; a new capture session is not historical input. The cutoff uses retained commit time strictly less than noon, not ACK time. Retained delayed writes, exact-C exclusion, same-millisecond sequence order, no-ops, withdrawals, absent entries, lawful post-C tails, lost ACK and postcommit disclosure uncertainty are modeled explicitly.

The only custody selector is `candidate_assignment`; no transferable ownership is implemented. `seed_authority` is always `unavailable`. Following-Saturday arithmetic is not proof of a selected seed, finality, chain incident or cancellation. No official event, portable authentication, GUI/D74, unbiased randomness or production wall-clock cutoff claim follows from this corpus. Genuine closed-cutoff helper composition may use the separately authorized scoped test clock, with its evidence label; the released bundle must retain ordinary clocks and normal PoW.
